correctness.rationale: For positive margins the polytope has the standard affine hull and a strictly positive feasible point. The orthogonal projection of E_ij onto the tangent space of zero row and column sums is (e_i-1/m)(e_j-1/n)^T, with squared Frobenius norm (m-1)(n-1)/(mn). Hence the centered-ball radius at X is exactly min_ij X_ij divided by this common norm. The maximum possible minimum entry is bounded by every row and column average and reaches their minimum t_* by subtracting t_* from every entry and filling the nonnegative residual margins with the product construction. The same equivalence gives the complete center set; the Birkhoff specialization follows exactly.

value.rationale: Transportation polytopes are a canonical family in polyhedral combinatorics and optimization. The theorem gives an exact Euclidean robustness radius for every positive margin vector, identifies every optimal center, and shows that a high-dimensional metric invariant depends only on the smallest normalized marginal. The Birkhoff inradius emerges as a sharp closed-form corollary. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary finite slice or recomputation.
